newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX seen hesistant before US data this week.
newsitem.headline: German DAX seen hesistant before US data this week.

text.p: German shares, languishing in late electronic trade on Tuesday, were expected to continue without direction through to at least Thursday, when the first of two key U.S. economic data were due to be published.
The IBIS-DAX index traded 11.10 points lower at 2,878.97 in late afternoon, after the main bourse index had earlier closed just ahead at 2,886.13.

"Investors are going through a re-orientation (of their portfolios) at the moment. We expect them to hold back until the end of the week, when the U.S. jobs and producer prices come through," said one dealer.
U.S. producer prices for December, due at 1330 GMT on Thursday, will be studied closely for signs of inflationary pressure that could influence decisions on U.S. rate movements.
U.S. payrolls data on Friday at the same time will also be examined for indications of the strength of the U.S. economy.
The latest German unemployment figures, due on Thursday, are expected only to influence German shares indirectly through the bond market, dealers said.
With little concrete corporate news around, a number of shares were pushed higher by resurfacing rumours of takeovers, particularly in the chemicals and drugs sectors.
In particular, Schering and Degussa were up three marks to 132.30 and five marks to 682 respectively on such speculation.
Schering was also said to have benefited from breaching a key resistance point of 129 marks.
